description: Declarative scorecard wording, scope and status corrections, consumed at build time by tools/control_diff.py, tools/scorecard.py, tools/summary_short.py, tools/build_lookup.py and tools/build_site.py. One entry per protocol slug; adding or updating a correction takes only an entry here and a rebuild. Pinned blocks are the historical observation blocks of the published records: no entry represents a fresh chain read. recordOverrides correct a record's published wording only: tools/apply_scorecard_corrections.py writes them (with the status and wording override maps) into docs/api/v1/index.json, and every attested field (id, block, hash, classification, summary document and its SHA-256, Base EAS UID, target, delays) is asserted unchanged; the audits/ summary documents are never touched.

statuses.unresolved: Observed on chain; a breach of a documented commitment is not established (neither Delta nor Aligned)
statuses.delta: Docs and chain differ (kept, with the corrected headline and scope)
statuses.recent_change: Changed on chain recently; documents not yet updated (observed within 48 hours of an on-chain change; re-checked after 72 hours before it counts as a Delta)

concrete.headline: ctDeltaWeETH: owner and manager roles share a 1-of-2 Safe; single-key full control or draining is not established
concrete.explanatorySentence: A 16 November snapshot of Concrete's Risks and Safety page describes separated roles preventing single-key full control or draining, while Pacta recorded ctDeltaWeETH's owner, VAULT_MANAGER and factory-manager authority in one 1-of-2 Safe at Ethereum block 26,425,374; this establishes concentrated manager authority, not a demonstrated single-key drain, and the page's current wording could not be verified. Separate role administrators, ConcreteFactory's 3-of-5 owner Safe and tiered Timelock implementation-approval controls, and strategy custody remain distinct checks.
concrete.summaryShort: ctDeltaWeETH owner/manager share a 1-of-2 Safe; single-key drain not established

lagoon.headline: Legacy cbBTC vault: immediate beacon upgrades; coverage by the documented 24-hour Opt-in delay is unverified
lagoon.explanatorySentence: Lagoon's Opt-in/DelayProxyAdmin documentation describes a 24-hour minimum upgrade wait (24 hours to 30 days), while Pacta's snapshot at Ethereum block 26,448,221 records a different, legacy cbBTC beacon-vault design controlled by a 3-of-6 Safe with no enforced wait on the recorded beacon upgrade path; whether that deployment is covered by the documented promise remains unverified.
lagoon.summaryShort: Legacy cbBTC beacon upgrades have no delay; 24h Opt-in doc coverage unverified

factorOverrides.timelock: 0s on the legacy cbBTC vault beacon upgrade path (3-of-6 Safe); whether the documented 24h Opt-in delay covers this vault is unverified

lagoon-vault-beacon-upgrade-delay-s29.surface: Legacy cbBTC vault beacon upgrades: no enforced delay under a 3-of-6 Safe; coverage by the 24 h Opt-in delay docs is unverified

renzo-protocol-ezeth.headline: DepositQueue fee parameter: 10,000 bps; effective reward fee and onward distribution are not verified
renzo-protocol-ezeth.explanatorySentence: Renzo documents a 10% restaking-reward fee, split equally between treasury and node operators (alongside separate EigenLayer-reward pass-through language), while Pacta recorded DepositQueue feeBasisPoints at 10,000 at Ethereum block 26,448,221, versus 1,500 at block 26,433,001; that parameter alone does not establish the effective fee on all ezETH rewards or who ultimately retains funds routed to feeAddress.
renzo-protocol-ezeth.summaryShort: DepositQueue feeBasisPoints reads 10,000 bps; effective fee and routing unverified

usual-money-usd0-usd0.headline: DEFAULT_ADMIN handover: one-second delay observed versus three days documented
usual-money-usd0-usd0.explanatorySentence: Usual documents three days before transferring DEFAULT_ADMIN to a new address, while Pacta recorded RegistryAccess defaultAdminDelay() as one second at Ethereum block 26,401,725; this finding concerns administrator handover, not a delay on every action by an existing administrator.
usual-money-usd0-usd0.summaryShort: DEFAULT_ADMIN handover delay: 1 second observed vs 3 days documented

factorOverrides.timelock: 1s DEFAULT_ADMIN role-handover delay (RegistryAccess.defaultAdminDelay); ordinary admin action delay not in published records

treehouse-tree-teth.headline: TREE transfer blacklisting: no enforced delay; TREE and tETH owner paths retain five-day timelocks
treehouse-tree-teth.explanatorySentence: Treehouse's Timelock documentation states that all Treehouse contracts are secured by a 5-day timelock so no critical action executes immediately, while Pacta recorded at Ethereum block 26,440,048 that a 5-of-7 Safe holds blacklister() on the TREE token with no enforced delay; TREE upgrade ownership (#26,406,106) and tETH ownership (#26,407,707) retain 5-day TimelockControllers.
treehouse-tree-teth.summaryShort: TREE blacklisting has no delay; TREE and tETH owner paths keep 5-day timelocks

factorOverrides.timelock: 0s on TREE token blacklisting (5-of-7 Safe); TREE and tETH owner/upgrade paths enforce a 5d timelock

beefy-finance-base.headline: Base vault-owner timelock: zero delay; strategy-owner changes retain six hours
beefy-finance-base.explanatorySentence: Beefy documents a 6-hour default timelock for strategy changes and upgrades alongside a general timelock assurance; at Base block 58,315,414 the sampled strategyOwner timelock enforces 6 hours while the Base vaultOwner timelock reads getMinDelay() = 0s.
beefy-finance-base.summaryShort: Base vault-owner timelock has zero delay; strategy-owner changes keep 6 hours

f-x-protocol-v2.headline: V2 Router owner is the operational Safe; the separate timelock retains three days
f-x-protocol-v2.explanatorySentence: f(x) Protocol documents a 3-day public timelock for queued transactions (with an oracle-update exception) and names LongPoolManager and ShortPoolManager for emergency pause; at Ethereum block 26,448,221 the V2 Router Diamond's owner() is the 6-of-9 operational Safe directly while the separate timelock retains three days (ProtocolTreasury role checks are distinct from the Long/ShortPoolManager pause promise).
f-x-protocol-v2.summaryShort: V2 Router owner is the 6-of-9 operational Safe; separate timelock keeps 3 days

gearbox-v3-v3-1.headline: LegacyTimelock reads 36 hours; V3.0 technical-change docs describe two days
gearbox-v3-v3-1.explanatorySentence: Gearbox's V3.0 operational-multisig documentation describes a 2-day timelock for technical changes (with exceptions) and notes chain-specific configuration for the 4-of-12 InstanceManager; at Ethereum block 26,403,523 the sampled LegacyTimelock reads delay() = 129,600s (36 hours per GIP-104).
gearbox-v3-v3-1.summaryShort: LegacyTimelock reads 36 hours; V3.0 technical-change docs describe 2 days

yearn-v3.headline: Sampled V3 RoleManager uses a seven-day timelock; yChad's documented signer roster differs
yearn-v3.explanatorySentence: At Ethereum block 26,441,165 the yChad Safe retains its 6-of-9 threshold while one address listed on the multisig documentation page is no longer an owner (consistent with an October 28 signer-rotation proposal, not a reduced threshold); separately, at block 26,401,725 a sampled V3 RoleManager points governance() to a 7-day TimelockController whereas Yearn's security overview notes the governance role itself is not behind a timelock.
yearn-v3.summaryShort: Sampled RoleManager uses a 7-day timelock; yChad signer roster differs (6-of-9)

yo-protocol.headline: Approval Registry is owned directly by the Admin Safe; vault upgrades retain a 48-hour timelock
yo-protocol.explanatorySentence: At Base block 58,315,414 YoApprovalRegistry owner() is the 4-of-6 Admin Multisig directly, while yoETH and yoUSD ProxyAdmins sit behind the 48-hour YO Timelock; the retained YO V2 Security Framework quote is from Pacta's Sprint 22 snapshot and was not re-verified against live docs today.
yo-protocol.summaryShort: Approval Registry owned by Admin Safe; vault upgrades keep a 48-hour timelock

tori-finance.headline: trUSD timelock: current documentation names the same 24-hour controller as the retained observation
tori-finance.explanatorySentence: At Ethereum block 26,451,608 Pacta recorded TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE on trUSD held by 24-hour ToriTimelock 0xcd3c66e73abF927EAAF1238aEB5F251b4f2f667b rather than 0xA952453E39F77108Ee37C1b92de593F1C59A6ef4; Tori Finance's retrieved roles documentation (21 November 2026) now names 0xcd3c66e73abF927EAAF1238aEB5F251b4f2f667b (86,400 seconds), resolving the document-side discrepancy pending a fresh finalized-block chain read.
tori-finance.summaryShort: trUSD timelock: current docs name the same 24-hour controller as observed
tori-finance.subtitle: Resolved by a documentation change; pending a fresh chain read
tori-finance.parityText: Current documentation names the retained 24-hour controller; pending a fresh chain read

whales-market.headline: Sampled Whales Market proxy is upgradeable; coverage by the pre-market escrow immutability promise is unverified
whales-market.explanatorySentence: Whales Market's pre-market buy guide states that deposited funds are stored in an escrow secured by an immutable smart contract, while Pacta recorded TransparentUpgradeableProxy slots on 0x1eCdB32e59e948C010a189a0798C674a2d0c6603 at Ethereum block 26,441,165; whether that proxy is the contract covered by the pre-market sell-order escrow statement is unverified.
whales-market.summaryShort: Sampled Whales Market proxy is upgradeable; escrow doc coverage is unverified

whales-market-upgradeability-s28.surface: Whales Market TransparentUpgradeableProxy: upgradeable; coverage by the pre-market escrow immutability statement is unverified

40-acres-base.headline: 40 Acres Base loan contract is upgradeable under a 2-of-3 Safe; its introduction describes contracts as immutable
40-acres-base.explanatorySentence: 40 Acres' introduction page states that smart contracts are immutable and non-upgradeable post-deployment, while Pacta recorded at Base block 59,025,642 that 0x87f18b377e625b62c708D5f6EA96EC193558EFD0 — listed on 40 Acres' contracts page as the AERO USDC Loan contract (distinct from the 0xB99B…7Cf5 Vault) — is a UUPS proxy owned by a 2-of-3 Safe.
40-acres-base.summaryShort: Base AERO USDC Loan contract is upgradeable (2-of-3 Safe); intro says immutable

40-acres-base-upgradeability-s28.surface: AERO USDC Loan contract (UUPS proxy): docs call the contracts immutable, but it is an upgradeable proxy

metamorpho-re7-weth-vs-re7-usdt.headline: Re7 WETH has no guardian; Re7 USDT has an Aragon guardian—no promise of matching configurations was verified
metamorpho-re7-weth-vs-re7-usdt.explanatorySentence: At Ethereum block 26,401,405 MetaMorpho Re7 WETH sets guardian() to the zero address under a 2-of-4 owner Safe and 3-day timelock, whereas peer vault Re7 USDT configures an Aragon guardian; Morpho's vault architecture explicitly supports vaults without a guardian and no Re7 documentation promising matching guardian configurations was verified.
metamorpho-re7-weth-vs-re7-usdt.summaryShort: Re7 WETH has no guardian while Re7 USDT does; no parity promise was verified
metamorpho-re7-weth-vs-re7-usdt.subtitle: Peer vault configuration differs; no documented parity promise verified
metamorpho-re7-weth-vs-re7-usdt.parityText: Peer vault comparison only; no documented promise of matching guardian configurations was verified

metamorpho-re7-weth-guardian-parity.documented_reference: Peer-vault configuration comparison (Re7 WETH vs Re7 USDT guardian settings); no Re7 documentation promising matching guardian configurations was verified, so this is not a broken documentation promise.

moonwell-lending-base.headline: Base pause guardian: 2-of-4 Safe, disclosed in the October governance migration; older constitution says 3-of-5
moonwell-lending-base.explanatorySentence: Moonwell's DAO Constitution (section 8.1) states that emergency pause actions require a 3-of-5 Security Council approval (while noting governance may modify council powers), whereas Unitroller.pauseGuardian() on Base resolved to a 2-of-4 Safe at block 57,842,915 — a configuration explicitly described in Moonwell's October 2026 governance forum recap of MIP-X71.
moonwell-lending-base.summaryShort: Base pause guardian is a 2-of-4 Safe (Oct MIP-X71); older constitution says 3-of-5

maple-finance-v2-syrup.headline: PoolPermissionManager proxy admin is the 4-of-7 DAO Safe, not GovernorTimelock
maple-finance-v2-syrup.explanatorySentence: Maple's Governor documentation places PoolPermissionManager implementation changes behind the Governor's delay, while Pacta's snapshot at Ethereum block 26,401,540 records that named proxy's admin as the 4-of-7 DAO Safe; this is a question about that proxy's upgrade route, not evidence that every Maple administrative action bypasses a three-day wait. (GovernorTimelock documentation specifies configurable delays with a 1-day minimum and discloses Security Admin exceptions; Maple's Token Transparency filing on Blockworks, section 3(b), states a 3-day GovernorTimelock for listed governance changes.)
maple-finance-v2-syrup.summaryShort: PoolPermissionManager proxy admin is the 4-of-7 DAO Safe, not GovernorTimelock

maple-v2-syrup-ppm-admin.documented_reference: Maple's Governor documentation places PoolPermissionManager implementation changes behind the Governor's delay; GovernorTimelock documentation specifies configurable delays with a 1-day minimum and discloses Security Admin exceptions; Maple's Token Transparency filing on Blockworks, section 3(b), states a 3-day GovernorTimelock for listed governance changes.

upshift.headline: Vault ProxyAdmin multisig: docs state generally 4 of 6, the Safe is 2-of-3
upshift.explanatorySentence: Upshift describes the ProxyAdmin Safe as generally 4-of-6 and discloses upgrades without a timelock, while Pacta recorded the ProxyAdmin owner of vault 0xE9B725010A9E419412ed67d0fA5f3A5f40159D32 as 2-of-3 at Ethereum block 26,441,165; the different signer count does not by itself show that one organization can upgrade alone.
upshift.summaryShort: Docs say ProxyAdmin is generally 4-of-6 (no timelock disclosed); vault's is 2-of-3

recentChangeRule.text: Any finding observed within 48 hours of an on-chain change carries Changed recently (changed on chain recently; documents not yet updated) and is re-checked after 72 hours before it counts as a Delta.
